full_judgment: 12. Mr. M. Aminul Islam, strenuously argued that a sentence of the said order regarding the date of taking the accused on police remand on 10th had been inserted subsequently which is evident from the fact that this sentence in the said order is seen to have been written above the mar-gin of the corresponding date written on the left hand column. We find no basis in his contention, firstly, because the appellant has not drawn the attention of P.W.8 in course of cross-examination by way of suggestion or otherwise that a sentence has been inserted later on, Secondly, he has not stated anything in this regard in reply to his examination under section 342, thirdly, this order has been written about 9 years before issuing the copy to the appellant and we find the writings of the entire order are the product of the same hand, and order has " been written with same ink, which could not have been possible if a sentence in the order has been inserted lateron after 9 years of passing the order, and finally, there is strong presumption in favour of regularity of performance of all judicial acts unless contrary is proved under illustration (E) to Section 114 of the Evidence Act. Therefore, there is no doubt that the appellant was taken on police remand on 10th and his confession was recorded of the following day of expiry of three days police remand. The order-sheet of the case supports the testimony of P.Ws.8 and 11. Thus, the contention of Mr. M. Aminul Islam has no substance at all.
